rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Table 3 - authors train KNN, SVM and ANN on a web-sourced irrigation dataset (wheat, maize, potato; 325 records), report classification accuracies (91%, 87%, 96.81%), and deploy the ANN on an Arduino/Raspberry Pi3 IoT setup described as tested in a potato and a wheat field.
rows.notes: The study's own results are the classification accuracy of three ML algorithms on a dataset scraped from the web (NIT Raipur), plus a one-sentence qualitative statement that the IoT system was tested in two fields and the pump opened only when irrigation was needed. No water applied, water saved or wastage is measured or compared with a conventional system, so there is no own evidence on the claimed effect (reducing water wastage); the study supports only the precondition that the system makes irrigate/not-irrigate decisions. No triangulation, mechanism measurement, multi-site evaluation of the effect, scale above plot, stated requirements, stated limitations, or dispersion measures for any water-saving result. The authors note field data from the Gharb region are still to be collected (future work).

notes: Full text appears complete. The paper is primarily an ML algorithm comparison on a public dataset; the field test is described in a single sentence without data.
